title: The Pulse, Tuesday 9 September 2026
tldr: OpenAI claims a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem with an AI-generated proof in Lean, drawing immediate scrutiny from mathematicians. Mistral raised €3B, the largest equity round in European tech history. Meta launched Muse, a personal AI agent with long-term memory; Addy Osmani joined Anthropic to work on Claude Code.

models.title: Inception: Mercury 2.5
models.summary: Diffusion LLM that generates and refines multiple tokens in parallel rather than sequentially, 4¢/M prompt tokens.
models.why: Parallel token generation could reduce latency for longer agent responses if the approach generalizes beyond the vendor's benchmarks.

models.title: Nex AGI: Nex-N2.5-Pro
models.summary: Free agentic coding model with visual feedback loop, multimodal input, 262k context.
models.why: Another free agentic coder joins the Claude Code / Codex competitive space; worth testing against our coding workflows.

research.title: When Does Memory Help? A Cost-Aware Evaluation of Long-Term Memory in Tool-Using LLM Agents
research.summary: MERIT benchmark measures whether remembered facts change what an agent does, not just conversational recall accuracy.
research.why: Directly relevant to our agent memory work in Hermes and Botterfly—evaluates if memory improves decisions, not just recall.

research.title: MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging
research.summary: Memory compression framework to reduce storage and retrieval costs during long-term agent inference.
research.why: Compression that preserves retrieval quality matters for production agents with accumulated context; applicable to our memory layer.

research.title: PARSER: Read in Parallel, Reason in Depth for Long-Context LLM Agents
research.summary: Decouples document reading from reasoning, processing chunks in parallel to reduce latency and evidence-placement sensitivity.
research.why: Parallel reading would help our retrieval-heavy flows in Pipeline's clients and SalesKick's call grading where documents are long.

research.title: Q2D-Web: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Retrieval in Agentic RAG Systems
research.summary: Benchmark pairing large-scale corpus with agent-reformulated search queries based on real conversations.
research.why: Tests retrieval in the way we actually use it—agents reformulating queries across conversation turns in production RAG.

releases.title: Node.js v24.21.0 'Krypton' (LTS)
releases.summary: LTS release with NSS 3.126 root certificates, OpenSSL 3.5.8, Undici 7.29.1, and performance improvements to net.BlockList.
releases.why: Our Next.js services and edge functions depend on current Node LTS; certificate and dependency updates matter for security.

releases.title: langchain-openai 1.6.1
releases.summary: Fixes Azure AD auth with OpenAI 3.8, adds async tools support and configuration_update, routes gpt-5.6-sol correctly.
releases.why: We use LangChain's OpenAI integration for SalesKick; async tools and routing fixes reduce integration friction.

releases.title: Langfuse v4.32.0
releases.summary: Alerts when a labeled preview is not serving, export data freshness metrics, fixes dataset metric reads when preview enabled.
releases.why: We rely on Langfuse observability for agent calls; alerting on broken previews and export freshness helps catch stale monitoring.

hackernews.title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
hackernews.summary: OpenAI claims an AI-generated solution to the Navier-Stokes problem with a formal proof in Lean; 1022 comments, significant mathematician skepticism.
hackernews.why: If verified, this reshapes what reasoning models can tackle; if not, it's a cautionary tale for publishing AI-generated proofs without peer review.

hackernews.title: Mistral raises €3B
hackernews.summary: Series D at €21B post-money valuation, three years after launch, largest equity round in European tech history.
hackernews.why: Mistral's open-weight models are on our evaluation list for cost-sensitive workloads; continued funding keeps them in the race.

hackernews.title: Muse – Meta's personal AI agent
hackernews.summary: Personal agent with long-term memory and proactive task suggestions, powered by Muse Spark 1.3.
hackernews.why: Meta entering personal agent space with memory shows the category maturing; patterns here apply to our assistant and scheduling work.

hackernews.title: I-have-ADHD: A skill to stop coding agents from burying the answer
hackernews.summary: Hermes skill forcing agents to lead with the answer and put context second; 360 points, resonated with agent users.
hackernews.why: This is a Hermes skill gaining traction in the wild—validates our agent framework and shows what users actually want from output structure.

x_posts.title: Addy Osmani joins Anthropic
x_posts.summary: Addy Osmani (ex-Google Chrome, developer tooling) announced he joined Anthropic to work on Claude Code.
x_posts.why: High-profile dev tooling hire signals Anthropic is deepening Claude Code investment; we track that product closely for coding workflows.

x_posts.title: GPT-Image-2.5 Flare and Sunburst
x_posts.summary: New image models in the OpenAI API with sharper detail, stronger style adherence, more control over edits.
x_posts.why: We use OpenAI's image models for content generation in campaigns; better style adherence reduces iteration cycles.

x_posts.title: Hermes in Omarchy
x_posts.summary: Hermes Agent now has first-class support in Omarchy, DHH's Arch-based agentic Linux distribution, with desktop app and CLI.
x_posts.why: Hermes is our agent framework; seeing it ship in a distro validates the approach and grows the ecosystem we're building on.
